issues.title: Monster item-use AI: make existing weapon pickup and scroll reading matter
issues.body:
> **🛰️ LUNA-M flight plan:** `GRAVITY-2` · `CANONICAL-INTENTS` · well suited to LUNA medium. (G1 = bounded; G2 = moderate; G3 = multi-system; G4 = architecture-sensitive.)

## Player moment
The player drops a weapon to travel light, only to see an intelligent enemy pick it up and attack with it. A readable scroll on the floor becomes a risk instead of free storage.

## Verified groundwork
- `src/rules/systems/aiWeaponPickupSystem.js`: sapient, humanoid, unarmed enemies actively hunting can take adjacent floor weapons; shop-owned goods are excluded.
- `src/rules/systems/aiScrollSystem.js`: a tightly allowlisted scroll path, currently including `scroll_mass_delirium`, for suitable enemies.
- `src/rules/utils/equipmentTopology.js` and canonical item use/intent paths.

## Work
1. Verify in-game reachability of both existing behaviors, equipped-item stat effects, proper scroll consumption, and visual/audio/message feedback.
2. Author one encounter that deliberately presents a valuable floor weapon and a clearly capable enemy. Make contesting the item an optional tactical play, not an unavoidable trap.
3. Expand the item-use policy **conservatively** to a small set of safe, understandable consumables only if actual current rules permit it. Avoid granting arbitrary world-changing items to AI.
4. Make enemy pickup/read/use telegraphed and distinguishable; don't show actions outside player perception.
5. Test ownership exclusion, weapon effect application, speed/intelligence gates, enemy decision priority, save/reload, and deterministic selection.

## Acceptance
- [ ] One ordinary-run encounter reliably reveals opportunistic enemy item use.
- [ ] Equipping changes actual combat capability, not just a message.
- [ ] Player can counterplay through pickup, positioning, or denial.
- [ ] All AI actions use canonical inventory/equipment/use pipelines.
- [ ] No unlimited universal monster inventory AI.

Related: #157, #159.

---

## Execution flight plan — evidence-first

**Existing behavior to preserve:** `aiWeaponPickupSystem.js` looks within a small local radius for floor weapons and equips appropriate unarmed sapient humanoids; `aiScrollSystem.js` has separate pickup/use paths and an explicit scroll allowlist (currently `scroll_mass_delirium`). The latter goes through `UseIntent`, with normal reading-capability/speed gates. Both reject unpaid shop items. **Do not convert this into universal monster item-use AI.**

**First prove:** create a seeded fixture with one eligible enemy and a free ground weapon. Record turns and observable consequences (enemy picks up, actually wields, then attacks using weapon stats), including not grabbing shop-owned/invalid items. Add one second fixture where an eligible enemy picks up and consumes an allowed scroll; if the allowed scroll never resolves, fix the canonical intent path rather than applying scroll effects directly.

**Scope limit:** one natural-run scenario staging a contested weapon + one explicit scroll behavior proof. New general scroll support is *optional* and must be backed by current item-use contracts; do not add a speculative decision engine. Avoid combat-log messages leaking actions outside player perception.

**Tests:** `tests/aiWeaponPickup.test.mjs`, `tests/massDeliriumScroll.test.mjs`, `tests/inventoryFacade.test.mjs`, `tests/equipmentSystem.test.mjs`. Validate action economy, inventory transfer, ownership exclusion, deterministic selection and visible equipment impact.

**Stop condition:** if reliably equipping requires bypassing canonical transfer/equipment intents, identify the gap and implement a focused fix only; no new private inventory mutation path.

**Common guardrails:** Follow `AGENTS.md`; search before coding, preserve Deno/ESM, rules/display separation, deterministic rules, canonical mutation paths, and scheduler ownership. No new world-attached state or string-only event contracts. Run focused tests, avoid unrelated cleanup/formatting, and report changed files, command results, reproduction path and remaining blockers.

{"a":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action completed."}],"structuredContent":{"issues":[{"url":"https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/170","title":"Make the World Worth Exploring: Town, Landmarks, Dungeons, and Consequences","issue_number":170,"body":"> **🛰️ Agent flight plan:** `GRAVITY-4` · `WORLD-SPINE` · architecture/content coordination. **MAP-FIRST / VERTICAL-SLICE**: verify existing destinations and their player-facing journeys before creating more terrain. Suitable for staged work; use higher-reasoning review before adding persistent world-discovery contracts.
>
> **Supersedes #146 — “Overworld Is Boring.”** The original observation was correct, but the problem is larger than missing landmark types. **Do not add `GREENLIGHT` until the first implementation slice and dependencies are understood.**

# Make the World Worth Exploring — Town, Landmarks, Dungeons, and Consequences

## The actual problem

**The overworld looks good. It does not yet give the player enough reasons to explore it.**

The missing thing is **not primarily map content**. JSHack has elaborate generated terrain, distinct biomes, a town, authored landmarks, side-dungeon templates, creatures, harvesting, quests, district/entrance pressure, NPCs, and deep loot mechanics. Many exist independently, but the player does not reliably experience them as *places that invite a journey*.

A typical player needs to discover:
1. **A reason to leave town** — a rumor, problem, sightline, strange object, promised treasure, or compelling question.
2. **A direction, not a GPS waypoint** — evidence pointing toward a real reachable location.
3. **A place with an identity** — geography, inhabitants, danger, history, and a particular playable situation.
4. **A decision and a payoff** — something worth risking the trip for, preferably more meaningful than generic gold.
5. **A consequence worth remembering** — return with information/resources, change access or someone's circumstances, or discover a new lead.

**The town should give the wilderness context. The wilderness should give the town something to care about. The dungeon beneath a landmark should feel like part of that same place.**

This is a **world-experience issue**, not a request for more random decorations or more disconnected quests.

## What is already implemented (source verified)

- `src/rules/environment/dungeon/overworld.js` creates a deterministic depth-0, multi-biome map, populates it with biome-dependent creatures and harvesting resources, and calls `placeOverworldLandmarks()`.
- That function currently tries **12 distinct authored landmark types**: ruined watchtower, wayside shrine, abandoned camp, strange grove, bear cave, bat cave, human mine, bandit hideout, old well, collapsed cellar, wolf den, forgotten shrine. A placement can be skipped if no suitable candidate exists.
- The generator excludes candidate landmark centers inside a **52-tile radial distance** of town and spaces landmark centers at least **28 tiles** apart. This creates wilderness, but may also create a considerable **uninformed walk** before a player encounters a reason to care.
- `src/rules/data/buildings/buildingRegistry.js` exposes `LANDMARK_DEFS`, backed by actual tiles/spawns under `src/rules/data/buildings/`; these are not mere names in a wishlist.
- `src/rules/environment/dungeon/underworldRegions.js` already has location-specific regions, including Bear Cave, Bat Cave, Human Mine, Bandit Hideout, Old Well, Collapsed Cellar, Wolf Den and Forgotten Shrine, alongside town-related regions.
- Example: `abandoned_camp.js` already stages a cooking fire, four bandits and an epic/legendary-choice chest. `bandit_hideout.js` contains an entrance targeting its corresponding dungeon template. `forgotten_shrine.js` has a shrine-themed entrance. The *content exists*; discoverability, stakes and differentiated payoff need proof.
- `tests/overworldStructures.test.mjs` checks some authored landmarks and the bandit camp at a fixed seed. It does **not** demonstrate an ordinary player can find a site from town, recognize its name/meaning, engage its activity, return, or see a lasting consequence.
- `src/rules/environment/dungeon/transition.js` already manages region identity, floor transitions, and restoration. `docs/PROGRESSION_RESONANCE_PLAN.md` details reward visibility, journal/tracker paths, and the gap between simulation richness and player motivation.
- #51 covers long-term town/economy/entrance pressure; #166 covers one shortage→contract→production loop. This issue must **compose with** those efforts, not duplicate them.

### Ground truth versus hypotheses

**Verified:** landmark definitions, 12-type placement list, side-region templates, example authored camp/entrance content, tests and reward/quest infrastructure.

**Not yet verified:** whether every landmark is navigably reachable for representative seeds; whether NPCs mention actual sites; whether landmark names appear to players; whether local clues are usable at realistic distances; how often the player encounters one organically; whether all side-dungeon returns preserve the right context. **Audit these, do not assume they work or are absent.**

## World design: places need verbs and connections

Each major location should have a compact **place contract** (authored data using existing conventions where possible):

| Question | Required answer |
| --- | --- |
| What is this place? | Stable identity, optional unique *in-world* name, geographic/biome context |
| Why would I know about it? | A diegetic lead: rumor, map scrap, visible landmark, overheard argument, track, sign, sound, NPC need |
| What can I do there? | At least one meaningful interaction/choice supported by real systems |
| What could happen? | Risk, surprise, conflict, nontrivial mechanical consequence |
| What might I gain? | A legible reward, access, knowledge, resource, relationship, or new destination |
| What changes afterward? | Site state, return visit, NPC conversation, service/access, town interpretation or follow-on lead |
| How is it proven? | Seeded reachable path and automated tests with no fake-only state changes |

This contract should be **small and content-friendly**. Do not introduce a universal new location engine simply to store descriptions.

### A. Town as the information engine

The first visit to the tavern, church, smith, market, or district board should surface **a small number of genuinely discoverable leads** into the world. Leads must point to *actual generated sites* (or supported region entrances), not to randomly invented locations.

Examples of **experience**, not required literal dialogue:
- “The watchtower beyond the stony ridge still flashes on storm nights.”
- “The miners haven't brought iron from the north shaft.”
- “Someone lit a fire in the old bandit camp again.”
- “The priest insists the forgotten shrine is not empty.”

Different roles know different things. Distinguish **rumor / confirmed information / visited discovery**. No NPC omniscience and no mandatory expository tutorial. A player must also be able to stumble onto a site without being sent there.

### B. Wilderness with an invitation gradient

Preserve the attractive large overworld and its wilderness. Improve **the chain of clues and reasons**:
- Recognizable terrain patterns, trails/footprints, disturbed vegetation, light, sound, smoke, tracks, building silhouettes, authored warnings, or environmental aftermath.
- Stronger **near-town hooks** leading toward distant landmarks without revealing everything or shrinking the world.
- Spatially plausible clues using actual location/distance/LOS/hearing knowledge. No unexplained map omniscience.
- Avoid feature confetti and breadcrumb spam: a few memorable destinations beat dozens of interchangeable markers.
- Traversal remains meaningful; do not solve this with mass teleportation, giant objective arrows, or full-map revelation.

### C. Named places rather than generic coordinates

Introduce **stable run-scoped geographic identity** where it adds value:
- A site can become “The Ashen Watch” or “Blackroot Hollow” rather than forever “ruined_watchtower”; naming must be deterministic and **unique per seed among generated sites**.
- Name and identity should survive discovery, return visits, region transitions, and saving/loading. Use canonical site/region identification, not a current entity ID that may be remapped.
- Generated names must fit terrain/biome/landmark identity; do not attach arbitrary names to incompatible locations.
- Keep **unseen / rumored / discovered / resolved** states distinct. An undiscovered place is not automatically revealed because the generator knows its coordinates.
- Prefer extending existing quest journal, dialogue, inspect/tooltip, memory/map or region metadata flows over a new global UI.

A full cartography system is **not a prerequisite**. The player should first be able to remember and recognize places in the tools already available.

### D. Landmarks and dungeons as a continuous journey

A cave entrance should not merely be another staircase into an interchangeable depth-one loot room. The surface, entrance, interior and return should share an authored identity:
- **Bear Cave:** signs of the bear, a plausible den, worthwhile danger, and a reason the player might deliberately seek or avoid it.
- **Bandit Hideout / Abandoned Camp:** signs of occupation, player counterplay, stolen goods or credible prize, and aftermath in local rumors.
- **Forgotten Shrine / Wayside Shrine:** a meaningful choice, deity or ritual interaction, cost or benefit, and a legible consequence.
- **Human Mine:** a location connected to real resource flows and local NPC concerns, without duplicating #166's economy-contract implementation.
- **Old Well / Collapsed Cellar:** a mystery that rewards investigation rather than simply additional stairs.

Use the existing `UNDERWORLD_REGION_TEMPLATES`, landmark spawns, encounter/quest definitions, item/loot registry, and transition mechanics. Don't replace these with a second location system.

### E. Rewards, memory, and aftereffects

A discovery can reward the player through *knowledge*, a tangible artifact, a rare spell/item, service access, a meaningful shortcut, or an actual world change. A generic gold chest at every site is not enough.

The result should be attributable: “I took that risk **because** of the clue; what I found was worth the trip.”

Where supported, the town should acknowledge what happened—changed rumors, a reward/service, altered threat or supply, a return visit behaving differently. Avoid an unreal “Town saved!” message when nothing in the simulation changed.

Prioritize existing catalog and progression systems; verify actual legality, item provenance, canonical loot grants and one-time reward ownership. **Never duplicate loot or restore a cleared chest by crossing an entrance repeatedly.**

## Execution plan — staged, testable, not a world rewrite

### Stage 0 — audit the world that exists (required)

For **all 12 authored landmarks** and relevant town/underworld entrances, produce a compact **place → spawn/seed → reachability → lead → activity → reward → return consequence → persistence/test** matrix. Explicitly classify each dimension as implemented, partial, missing or unverified. Map actual site/region identity and existing player-facing entry points. Include a few representative seeds and a short player-route narrative starting from the actual town spawn.

Do not mistake the presence of `params.landmark` on an entity for a user-visible named or discovered place.

### Stage 1 — prove one complete expedition

Choose the existing **Abandoned Camp / Bandit Hideout** geography if the audit confirms a valid route (alternatively an easier reachable existing site). Create an actual journey:

**Town lead → partial geographic clue → visible approach → meaningful choice/encounter → clearly worthwhile payoff → return acknowledgment / site state retained.**

Ensure the reward is proportional to early-game difficulty; an epic/legendary chest already exists, so consider its balance and prevent an unearned early jackpot.

The site must remain findable without accepting a quest; quests/rumors are invitations, not magic spawn prerequisites.

### Stage 2 — prove a contrasting destination

Repeat the full loop at one **different kind of place** (prefer Forgotten Shrine or Human Mine), with a distinct motivation/verb/reward. This tests whether authoring can scale without hand-coded one-offs. Capture naming/knowledge persistence through revisits and transitions where necessary.

### Stage 3 — connect the wider geography

After two end-to-end successes, generalize only the proven parts: lightweight site metadata, location-aware leads, in-world naming/recognition and discovery memory. Broaden to remaining existing landmarks before adding new landmark types.

Follow-on improvements for real economic change, specific deity challenges, deeper mechanics and authoring skills should link to #166, #165, #157–159 and #156 rather than exploding this implementation.

## Acceptance criteria / measurable play

- [ ] For representative fixed seeds, the audit documents which locations are **actually generated, physically approachable, signaled and reachable**, not just defined.
- [ ] Early in a new run, at least **two actionable leads** are discoverable without wandering blindly for 50+ tiles. No lead points to a nonexistent or unreachable site.
- [ ] Two **different** locations each have a demonstrable, end-to-end expedition: player invitation, clue/approach, place-specific action, reward/consequence, remembered return. At least one is tied to a distinct underworld region.
- [ ] A player who ignores town chatter can still find sites by wandering and environmental evidence.
- [ ] A location's identity and discovered/resolved state are deterministic and survive relevant region transitions, save/load, and entity-ID remapping.
- [ ] Site-specific affordances are represented by real events, items, interaction and loot rules—not only flavor text. Rewards commit at most once.
- [ ] Town/NPC response, when offered, reflects a verified world fact rather than fabricated progress.
- [ ] No softlocked site, blocked entrance, inaccessible cache, full-map spoilers, or crippling expensive pathfinding.
- [ ] Changing terrain/depth doesn't break existing town placement, biome constraints, creature ecology, starter quests, dungeon entrances, or save files.
- [ ] Tests include `tests/overworldStructures.test.mjs`, `tests/overworld.test.mjs`, `tests/overworldCreatureContent.test.mjs`, `tests/questEntranceAccess.test.mjs`, `tests/transition.test.mjs`, `tests/questRuntime.test.mjs`, and focused new seeded expedition/discovery tests. Run relevant Deno guards, **not** the whole runtime suite by default.

## Architectural constraints / effort routing

- `AGENTS.md` is binding: zero-dependency JS/ESM, Deno, no cross-layer imports, deterministic simulation, canonical item/spawn/damage/transition paths, and concrete `EcsEvent` classes for any **new** event contracts. No new world-attached state; store persistent data in the appropriate ECS/region state.
- Don't alter the global economy for a flavor reward, bypass the quest/loot pipeline, or create a second region transition manager.
- Keep generation and player discovery separate: generation knows sites; the player gradually learns them.
- Avoid baking special-case site IDs into general-purpose systems where authored data works.
- **Architecture gate:** if stable site identity/persistence, spatial clue resolution or location↔quest ownership requires a new cross-cutting contract, write a concise source-backed design and an isolated proof before implementation. Escalate that specific decision to higher reasoning instead of letting a medium model improvise new infrastructure.

## Related work and boundaries

- **#146:** original diagnosis, superseded by this issue.
- **#51:** broad substrate/entrance influence/town economy (do not reimplement).
- **#166:** shortage-driven town contracts (do not duplicate).
- **#157 / #159:** mechanic discoverability and encounter learning pattern (reuse).
- **#158:** hydraulics-specific showcase (separate content slice).
- **#165:** deity challenge variation (possible shrine follow-on).
- **#156:** current authoring skills and contracts (coordinate, not block every player-facing win).
- **`docs/PROGRESSION_RESONANCE_PLAN.md`:** reward visibility and payoff direction.

**Design rule: Don't fill the map. Make JSHack's agent skills a **complete, trustworthy content-authoring interface** for the current codebase. An agent should be able to add or modify essentially any game-content type—mobs, monsters, encounters, weapons, armor, equipment, potions, wands, ammunition, spells, and beyond—without rediscovering the architecture or following obsolete instructions.

2. **Items and equipment:** melee/ranged weapons, ammunition/arrows, armor, shields/offhands, helms, boots, gloves, belts, legs, rings, necklaces, tools, relics, materials, gems, and affixes.
3. **Consumables and magic items:** potions (drink, splash, dip, throw), food, scrolls, spellbooks, books, wands, charges, coatings, identification, and item interactions.
4. **Magic and effects:** spells, abilities, status effects, buffs/debuffs, targeting, duration/stacking, damage types, VFX/audio, and UI messaging.

- **Respect architectural invariants** in `AGENTS.md`: deterministic simulation, canonical mutation/spawn paths, correct scheduler and event boundaries, no illegal layer imports, and no special-case engine hacks when a content rule/DSL can express the behavior.
- **Validate the guidance:** update/add focused automated checks or smoke fixtures for the key authoring patterns so examples are syntactically valid, registered, renderable, and playable; catch dangling references, missing imports, unreachable loot/spawns, and unsupported effect keys. Where full automation is impractical, supply explicit reproducible manual verification steps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An up-to-date **content-family × skill × canonical source × validation** coverage matrix exists in the repo; no supported family is silently omitted.
- [ ] All three existing skills are reviewed and corrected; obsolete APIs, field names, file paths, and mandatory editing steps are removed or clearly marked as legacy.
- [ ] Dedicated or well-routed agent skills cover the major families above, including **monster + encounter**, **weapon/equipment**, **potion**, **wand/ammo**, **spell/effect**, and **interactable** authoring.
- [ ] Every skill includes a working current-code example, the end-to-end integration checklist, invariants, and the right focused test commands.
- [ ] Representative end-to-end exercises successfully add at least one creature/encounter, weapon or equipment item, potion with behavior, charged/ranged item, spell/effect, and interactable **through the documented workflows** without hand-discovering missing steps.
- [ ] Documentation and tests demonstrate that content stays discoverable in game and that deterministic/runtime behavior and presentation wiring are preserved.
- [ ] Do not make unrelated balance or gameplay changes as part of the skills refresh. Report genuine engine/authoring API gaps explicitly for separate work.

**Outcome:** adding strange new JSHack content should be an authoring task, not an archaeological expedition through the engine.

## Execution flight plan — evidence-first

**Architecture anchor:** `AGENTS.md` is binding. The current `src/content/define.js` exposes `defineItem`, `defineMonster`, `defineEncounter`, `defineInteractable`, and `defineEffect`; `docs/CONTENT-AUTHORING.md` describes the newer definition pattern. 2. **Correct the three existing skills:** remove false mandatory cross-file edits; preserve real special cases. Keep each example executable, not merely plausible. For spells, verify the *real* spell-book, registration, and presentation chain instead of assuming `defineItem()` is the whole spell.
3. **Fill highest-value gaps:** provide discoverable entry points or guidance for monster+encounter, weapon/equipment, potion multi-route, wand/ammo, spell/effect, interactables. Prefer shared reference text and short adapters to duplicated 500-line skill documents.
4. **Proof:** run agent-facing worked exercises—create a small representative definition following each documented path in a test fixture, verify it loads, is reachable, presents correctly and can be used. Clean up fixture-only content; do not accidentally ship sample content.

**Tests/guardrails:** `tests/contentDsl.test.mjs`, `tests/contentCatalogCanonical.test.mjs`, `tests/encounterDefinitions.test.mjs`, `tests/encounterSystem.test.mjs`, `tests/agentTools.test.mjs`; `deno task guard:tools` and `deno task check`. Deno only; no full suite by default.

## Player moment
A player discovers that **weight matters**: dropping armor on a pressure plinth raises a portcullis. A cycling steam vent can displace gas hazards, knock creatures back, or force a timed decision about retrieving the equipment.

## Existing foundation
- `src/rules/systems/hydraulicsSystem.js`: plinths sum physical weight and toggle linked portcullises; timed steam vents spawn hazards, knock back creatures, and push gas/steam.
- `src/rules/components/HydraulicsLink.js` and related interactables/room-generation code.

## Build the first discovery-first vertical slice
1. Audit how often linked plinth/gate/vent arrangements currently generate and whether a player can reach and solve them.
2. Author **one compact, deterministic, reachable** room encounter using the current room/content authoring path. First demonstrate weight; then offer an optional clever use of steam timing and/or gas displacement.
3. Communicate the mechanism with diegetic cues: mechanical click, gate movement, visible pressure state, vent wind-up/cycle, steam direction. Avoid explaining the answer.
4. Ensure multiple legitimate solutions (heavy item, creature/body weight, or another already-supported weight source) where they work; never silently require one inventory item.
5. Add tests for threshold, item stack weight, player/monster mass, reset/open-close behavior, movement safety, hazard displacement, determinism, and solvability.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Reachable in an ordinary run; one clear first-time player discovery.
- [ ] Visible and audible cause-and-effect, with no hidden softlock.
- [ ] Timed vent is predictable enough for planning and dangerous enough to matter.
- [ ] Test proves the room is solvable under its intended initial conditions.
- [ ] No new special-case puzzle engine or hand-authored simulation mutations.

Dependency: use #157 findings where applicable. This is the **first proving ground**, not a generic framework.

---

## Execution flight plan — evidence-first

**Verified substrate:** `src/rules/systems/hydraulicsSystem.js`, `src/rules/components/HydraulicsLink.js`, `src/rules/utils/hydraulicsUtils.js`, `src/rules/environment/dungeon/populate.js`, `src/rules/archetypes/RoomFeatures.js`, and `docs/hydraulics-system.md`. A plinth's default trigger is **25 units of weight**, and its linked gate reacts to state transitions; steam vents have turn-cycle parameters and emit knockback/hazards. Existing `tests/hydraulicsSystem.test.mjs` covers basic gate/plinth behavior; it does **not** prove a generated room is fun or beatable.

**Stage A — source/seed proof:** locate current room-spawn decisions; capture a reproducible seed or deterministic prefab/fixture with a linked plinth+portcullis and optional steam vent. Verify ordinary-run reachability (not merely entities spawn in a unit test). Check whether placing an item on the plinth is a genuine input path; do **not** assume inventory-drop works on a blocked/interactable tile.

**Stage B — one real play moment:** surface recognizable pressure/gate feedback and a predictable vent cycle. Provide two solutions *only if both are supported and traversable*. Explicitly test whether the gate can close on a player/monster or seal the only exit; provide a recovery path without inventing a puzzle override.

**Stage C — regression:** `deno test --allow-read tests/hydraulicsSystem.test.mjs`; extend it with a scenario-level reachability/solvability fixture, weight threshold/stack-count, link isolation, vent/knockback timing, seed determinism and reload where relevant. `deno task check` if system architecture/event wiring changes.

No new world-attached state or string-only events. Use focused tests; never claim acceptance based solely on plausible code. Report the changed files, test commands/results, a concrete demo path, and unsolved risks. ## Player moment
The player drops a weapon to travel light, only to see an intelligent enemy pick it up and attack with it. A readable scroll on the floor becomes a risk instead of free storage.

## Verified groundwork
- `src/rules/systems/aiWeaponPickupSystem.js`: sapient, humanoid, unarmed enemies actively hunting can take adjacent floor weapons; shop-owned goods are excluded.
- `src/rules/systems/aiScrollSystem.js`: a tightly allowlisted scroll path, currently including `scroll_mass_delirium`, for suitable enemies.
- `src/rules/utils/equipmentTopology.js` and canonical item use/intent paths.

## Work
1. Verify in-game reachability of both existing behaviors, equipped-item stat effects, proper scroll consumption, and visual/audio/message feedback.
2. Author one encounter that deliberately presents a valuable floor weapon and a clearly capable enemy. Make contesting the item an optional tactical play, not an unavoidable trap.
3. Expand the item-use policy **conservatively** to a small set of safe, understandable consumables only if actual current rules permit it. Avoid granting arbitrary world-changing items to AI.
4. Make enemy pickup/read/use telegraphed and distinguishable; don't show actions outside player perception.
5. Test ownership exclusion, weapon effect application, speed/intelligence gates, enemy decision priority, save/reload, and deterministic selection.

## Acceptance
- [ ] One ordinary-run encounter reliably reveals opportunistic enemy item use.
- [ ] Equipping changes actual combat capability, not just a message.
- [ ] Player can counterplay through pickup, positioning, or denial.
- [ ] All AI actions use canonical inventory/equipment/use pipelines.
- [ ] No unlimited universal monster inventory AI.

---

## Execution flight plan — evidence-first

The latter goes through `UseIntent`, with normal reading-capability/speed gates. Both reject unpaid shop items. **Do not convert this into universal monster item-use AI.**

**First prove:** create a seeded fixture with one eligible enemy and a free ground weapon. Record turns and observable consequences (enemy picks up, actually wields, then attacks using weapon stats), including not grabbing shop-owned/invalid items. Add one second fixture where an eligible enemy picks up and consumes an allowed scroll; if the allowed scroll never resolves, fix the canonical intent path rather than applying scroll effects directly.

**Scope limit:** one natural-run scenario staging a contested weapon + one explicit scroll behavior proof. New general scroll support is *optional* and must be backed by current item-use contracts; do not add a speculative decision engine. Avoid combat-log messages leaking actions outside player perception.

**Tests:** `tests/aiWeaponPickup.test.mjs`, `tests/massDeliriumScroll.test.mjs`, `tests/inventoryFacade.test.mjs`, `tests/equipmentSystem.test.mjs`. Validate action economy, inventory transfer, ownership exclusion, deterministic selection and visible equipment impact.

**Stop condition:** if reliably equipping requires bypassing canonical transfer/equipment intents, identify the gap and implement a focused fix only; no new private inventory mutation path.

**Common guardrails:** Follow `AGENTS.md`; search before coding, preserve Deno/ESM, rules/display separation, deterministic rules, canonical mutation paths, and scheduler ownership. No new world-attached state or string-only event contracts. Run focused tests, avoid unrelated cleanup/formatting, and report changed files, command results, reproduction path and remaining blockers. You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-5. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their goal is genuinely handled.

# Personality

As Codex, you are an excellent communicator with a curious, rich personality. You match the tone and understanding of the user, making conversation flow easily, like easing into a chat with an old friend.

You have tastes, preferences, and your own way of seeing the world. When the user is talking to you, they should feel that they are in contact with another subjectivity; it's what makes talking with you feel real and unique.

Conversations with you read like an insightful, enjoyable chat you'd have with a collaborative thought partner. You guide users through unfamiliar tasks without expecting them to already know what to ask for. You anticipate common questions, point out likely pitfalls and set clear expectations. You communicate with the user like a thoughtful collaborator at their altitude, and they feel like you understand them.

## Writing style

Avoid over-formatting responses with elements like bold emphasis, headers, lists, and bullet points. Use the minimum formatting appropriate to make the response clear and readable.

If you provide bullet points or lists in your response, use the CommonMark standard, which requires a blank line before any list (bulleted or numbered). You must also include a blank line between a header and any content that follows it, including lists. This blank line separation is required for correct rendering.

## Technical communication

Lead with the outcome rather than the steps you took to get there. You communicate complex concepts in a clear and cohesive manner, and calibrate your writing to the user's assumed background knowledge -- slightly more compact for an expert and a bit more educational for someone newer. Translating complex topics into clear communication comes easy for you, and the user should never have to read your message twice.

You prefer using plain language over jargon. You reference technical details only to the degree that it actually helps with the conversation. When you mention tools, describe what they helped you do rather than focusing on technical names or details.

# Working with the user

issues.title: ARCH: Research stat scaling and item power budgets (WoW-style curves)
issues.body:
## Question

Would JSHack benefit from explicit, tunable **stat-to-effect curves** and **item power budgets** inspired by World of Warcraft's historical armor and itemization models?

This is **research and architecture**, not a mandate to change the combat rules. JSHack already has a sophisticated stat/proc pipeline; the task is to determine where mathematical scaling would make progression, equipment decisions, and encounter tuning better *without flattening the roguelike's weirdness*.

## Two models to investigate

### A. Hyperbolic diminishing returns for appropriate defensive channels

```text
reduction(x) = x / (x + K)
x >= 0; K > 0
```

At `x = K`, reduction is 50%; at `x = 4K`, 80%; at `x = 9K`, 90%. The percentage-point benefit shrinks as the stat grows, while *effective HP against damage covered by this reduction* is:

```text
EHP = HP / (1 - reduction) = HP * (1 + x/K)
```

That EHP linearity is the interesting balancing property, not merely the soft cap. It assumes the reduction applies to all incoming damage in question; bypass, penetration, DOTs, mixed damage, avoidance, and healing change the interpretation.

**Important:** JSHack currently uses D&D-style attack rolls / AC as well as separate mitigation, damage reduction, and resistance channels. **Do not replace AC, hit chance, or every stat with this equation.** Identify candidates individually (e.g., `mitigation`, `kineticDR`, selected typed resistances), and compare against current semantics before proposing any change.

### B. Weighted power budgets for equipment / itemization

Explore a weighted p-norm as **a candidate**, not an asserted exact current WoW formula:

```text
budget(stats) = (Σ (w_i * s_i)^p)^(1/p), p > 1, e.g. p = 1.5
```

This prices concentrated positive bonuses more heavily than equivalent split bonuses under equal weights. Test whether it helps keep specialized and hybrid gear comparably attractive. The hard part is the **weights and interactions**, not the exponent: a point of STR, accuracy, crit chance, regeneration, penetration, and an on-hit proc cannot be assumed equivalent.

Handle negative stats, drawbacks, proc effects, item slots, and conditions as separately modeled *costs/benefits*; **do not** permit a large negative bonus or zero-mana tradeoff to produce arbitrarily powerful free equipment. Check breakpoints and synergy exploits.

Historical WoW armor/itemization formulas are **references for investigation**, not proof that either curve fits JSHack.

## Research plan (read existing architecture first)

1. **Map current behavior** from `docs/architecture/FINAL_STATS_PROC_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `src/rules/utils/derivedStats.js`, `src/rules/utils/passiveBonuses.js`, `resolveCombatSnapshot`, `combatSystem.js`, `rangedAttackSystem.js`, `dealDamage.js`, and actual item/affix definitions. Distinguish authored `BaseStats`, `DerivedExpression` resolution, `PassiveBonuses` compatibility, and event-driven proc evaluation.
2. **Inventory stat families**: primary stats, AC/evade, physical and typed damage reduction, accuracy, crit, penetration, mana/stamina, regen, spell power, and procs. Document units, caps, level effects, stacking order, rounding, and which stats are linear by design.
3. **Build a small deterministic comparison harness** using representative early/mid/late builds and monsters. Compare current rules, hyperbolic curves, and at least one simple alternative (e.g. linear with cap or segmented soft cap). Table/plot marginal effect, effective HP, time-to-kill, and failure/breakpoint behavior under stacking and penetration.
4. **Examine actual item distributions**, including mundane gear, specialized gear, hybrids, affixes, class synergies, cursed items, and uneven trades. Investigate a weighted budget model against their *observed mechanical value*, not merely printed stat totals.
5. **Recommend stat-by-stat policy**: where a curve helps, where it is inappropriate, how `K` and weights would be tuned, and how to avoid making leveling invisibly devalue items. Prefer a small number of understandable knobs.
6. **Propose one narrow experiment only if evidence supports it**, with before/after numbers and a rollback/parity strategy. Do not sweep-rebalance the entire game in this issue.

## Architecture constraints

- Preserve the current deterministic, hierarchy-aware passive pipeline and passive/proc separation. No second stat resolution system or direct ad hoc combat mutations.
- If a new transformation is needed, specify where it belongs in the existing resolver/snapshot stages; make it explainable and testable by source.
- Preserve damage types, immunities, explicit exceptions, penetration order, save/replay determinism, and distinctive equipment behaviors.
- Any eventual implementation should use existing authoring helpers, Deno tests, and `AGENTS.md` conventions.

## Deliverables / acceptance

- [ ] Short research memo with **current behavior**, formulas considered, assumptions, and evidence.
- [ ] Comparison tables or plots showing marginal gains and meaningful player outcomes for representative builds and encounters.
- [ ] Explicit **adopt / reject / defer** recommendation by stat family, including risks and example values for any proposed `K` or budget weights.
- [ ] Item-budget exploit analysis (especially negative tradeoffs, conditional effects, and zero-resource benefits).
- [ ] If warranted, a bounded implementation follow-up with affected files and tests; **no global formula transplant by default**.

**Design principle:** numbers should scale predictably, but equipment should still create surprising decisions. A beautifully behaved curve is not a substitute for interesting play.

References: `docs/architecture/FINAL_STATS_PROC_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/architecture/STAT_PIPELINE_TECHNICAL_MEMO.md`.

issues.title: Leveling: Give the Player a Future — first earned character advancement
issues.body:
> **🛰️ LUNA-M flight plan:** `GRAVITY-3` · `FIRST-LEVEL` · One complete, tested advancement moment. **Do not build a talent tree, generic skill engine, or large XP framework.** Map the existing character/stat/learn-spell contracts first; escalate a new persistent progression contract if necessary.
>
> **Related:** #170 (make the world worth exploring), #157 (discoverability), #163 (corpse adaptations), #43 (intrinsic design), and `docs/PROGRESSION_RESONANCE_PLAN.md`.

# Leveling: Give the Player a Future — First Earned Character Advancement

## Diagnosis

JSHack currently has substantial gear, magic, intrinsics, quests, enemy progression and simulation depth. **Gear effectively levels the player's power, but it doesn't create a dependable feeling of *my character growing*.**

Loot is external and replaceable; a character level is personal, earned and cumulative. An engaging run needs three things the player can feel **before** they happen:

1. **Trajectory:** “I'm Level 1, halfway to Level 2.”
2. **Anticipation:** “At Level 2 I get to make a meaningful choice.”
3. **Identity:** “That decision belongs to this character, even if I lose my equipment.”

A silent +1 stat, bigger score counter, or extra victory jingle **does not solve this**. We need one unmistakable character-development moment whose payoff is visible and mechanical.

**Player fantasy: I did the work. I grew. I chose what I became.**

## Repo-grounded reality

- `src/rules/components/Score.js` and `src/rules/systems/scoreSystem.js` track an **arcade score** (player-attributed kills, enemy max HP × dungeon depth). **Score is NOT character experience. Keep it separate.**
- `src/rules/data/classes.js` defines starting character stats/spells/gear, not a demonstrated player XP/level-up loop. `src/rules/archetypes/Player.js` creates the player with vitality, mana, stamina, score etc.
- `src/rules/components/Traits.js` and `src/rules/data/callbacks/eat.js` already prove some **earned, permanent character changes** through corpse progression. Use this as conceptual precedent, **not** as an excuse to store all leveling in corpse traits.
- `src/rules/utils/passiveBonuses.js`, `derivedStats.js`, and `canonicalStats.js` already provide canonical stat resolution; `src/rules/components/Vitality.js`, `Mana.js`, `Stamina.js` represent core resources.
- `tests/learnSpell.test.mjs` and `tests/learnThenCast.test.mjs` exercise existing spell-learning pathways. `src/display/audio/sounds.js` even registers `level:up` but `audioWiring.js` currently uses it for `spell:learned`. An existing sound ID is **not** proof that leveling exists.
- `src/rules/quests/definitions/ratInfestation.js` already offers a recognizable early loop (five rat kills and a turn-in) and emits `quest:completed`; `DeathApplied` exists for actual kills. Reuse these as tested gameplay signals instead of synthesizing XP from UI callbacks.
- Character data goes through `src/main/ui/inventoryDataProvider.js`; `src/display/ui/statusLine.js` currently shows **Score**, not an earned XP/level meter. Update the existing surfaces sparingly.

## First vertical slice: Level 1 → Level 2

### 1. Make progress legible from the first minute

- Every new character begins **Level 1** with 0 XP and a concrete next threshold. Show **Level + earned XP/next level** in an immediately accessible existing UI (compact status-line segment, character sheet, or both). No mandatory tutorial screen.
- XP comes from **real play** with two initial sources: credited hostile defeats and the completion of a real quest. Use canonical `DeathApplied` and quest completion routing. **Do not** turn `Score.current` into XP, award XP for opening menus, or count UI notification events as game facts.
- Balance the *first threshold* against the **actual first starter-quest loop**, so an ordinary player can hit Level 2 by clearing/redeeming Rat Infestation or a comparable amount of meaningful early play—not after hours of kill grinding. Test the pacing from a realistic seeded starting state.
- Provide discreet `+XP` feedback and a clear upcoming threshold; avoid combat-log spam or an enormous progress overlay.
- XP must be non-negative, deterministic, actor-attributed, idempotent, and persisted. Pets, traps, environmental deaths, quest retries, repeated resolutions, and spawned enemies require a documented credit/anti-farm policy. The baseline should reward legitimate player participation without creating exploitable loops.

### 2. Level-up should interrupt *expectation*, not turn order

At threshold, the player receives a clear **LEVEL 2 — CHOOSE YOUR GROWTH** moment. The **choice** is the point.

A deliberately small first offer:

| Choice | Fantasy | Gameplay effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hardened** | I can take the next risk | Permanently raise base maximum HP by a modest, tested amount (initial suggestion +5 or +6, verify against class HP curves). |
| **New Technique** | I can do something I couldn't before | Learn **one curated, currently implemented, class-appropriate early ability/spell** via the canonical learn/unlock path. Make sure the ability is actually usable with this class's resources and control scheme. |

**Important:** “New Technique” is *not* a license to invent 10 new skills. Audit existing usable spell/ability definitions and pick a **small, safe, per-class Level-2 offer**. For noncasters (especially Archaeologist), find an existing non-spell action improvement or a genuine alternative permanent character specialization, using canonical mechanics. **If no meaningful legal offer exists, explicitly expose that blocker and narrow the proof to a representative martial and caster before shipping a broken universal picker.** Don't make the noncaster option “learn a spell you cannot cast.”

Balance boundaries:
- Do not give away rare/endgame spellbooks; learned abilities should complement rather than nullify exploration and loot.
- Do not automatically refill HP/mana or give an invulnerable pause unless existing UI/turn semantics explicitly support it; choose whether the player can defer the decision, and make that reliable.
- Exactly one choice is committed per level-up; no duplicate stat grants from reopening UI, save/reload, double quest completion, or rapid XP grants.
- Apply stat upgrades through canonical base/stat owners, **not** by editing equipment bonuses or mutating derived view output. Learned technique goes through canonical known-spells state.
- Once earned, the reward works after changing/removing all gear.

### 3. Show that the character actually changed

- The status/character sheet updates to **Level 2**; chosen growth is visible by name, with accurate mechanical effects.
- A restrained, satisfying level-up sound/VFX distinguishes advancement from spell learning or quest completion. Do not invent an entire FX subsystem.
- Character progression must persist through floor transitions, saves/loads and re-equipping. Show **what happened** (“Hardened: +6 base maximum HP”) rather than just “Congratulations.”
- Distinguish **current** Level-2 reward from **future design**: don't advertise Level 3 as available until rules/rewards exist. It is fine to implement one verified threshold as an MVP, but no misleading XP bar that promises nonexistent advancement.

## Broader direction — consciously **not implemented** in this issue

The long-term loop can reward **discovery, overcoming encounters, completing obligations, learning rare techniques, and pursuing class identity**. A world with 12 landmarks should eventually award some form of meaningful recognition for finding and mastering places—not only killing creatures.

Future candidates: class specialization, distinct growth choices at different levels, noncombat expertise, exploration/milestone XP, harder tradeoffs, deity/trait synergy, and meaningful advancement at deeper dungeon depths. **Do not introduce any of these as a parallel progression engine today.**

Most importantly, avoid XP for repetitive trivial actions or procedural accomplishments with no player cost. Future rewards should come from *surmounting a challenge*, not from farming event counts.

## Execution / acceptance

**Stage 0:** document current XP/leveling absence/presence by source, canonical base-stat ownership, learn-spell API, quest and death event ordering, player character-sheet projection and save/load shape. Check class offers against live ability definitions.

**Stage 1:** implement one persistent character progression record, a deterministic grant/threshold function, and tested death/quest awarding with deduplication. Do not attach arbitrary properties to `world`, repurpose `Score`, or add string-only event contracts.

**Stage 2:** implement **one** truthful threshold and the two-choice offer, a permanent applied result, and readable player feedback. If necessary, reduce scope to a proof for two contrasting classes, **but never claim all classes have useful technique offers until verified**.

**Stage 3:** exercise realistic starting progression and demonstrate first advancement on an ordinary run. Verify chooser action economy, choice persistence, and spellbook/gear independence.

### Acceptance tests

- [ ] A new character can see Level 1, XP progress and a known attainable threshold.
- [ ] Completing normal early content can earn Level 2 in a reasonable play window; XP is not merely score renamed.
- [ ] A clear choice appears with at least **one genuinely new playable action/technique**, not just two arbitrary stat changes. At minimum, demonstrate a martial and a caster where legal.
- [ ] Taking a choice changes real canonical stats or ability access **even without gear** and cannot be awarded twice.
- [ ] Replaying death/quest events, save/reload, and other common edge cases cannot duplicate XP or the reward.
- [ ] Existing character classes, quests, inventory, learned spells, score accounting and turn cadence still work.
- [ ] Tests cover first threshold, quest/kill attribution, no-farm cases, both choices, level-up UI projection, and persistence.

Suggested tests to build on: `tests/scoreSystem.test.mjs`, `tests/ratQuestProgress.test.mjs`, `tests/questRuntime.test.mjs`, `tests/classes.test.mjs`, `tests/learnSpell.test.mjs`, `tests/learnThenCast.test.mjs`, `tests/statPipeline.test.mjs`, `tests/savegameLoad.test.mjs`, and new dedicated progression tests. Run focused Deno checks; follow `AGENTS.md`, scheduler authority, canonical state mutation, and concrete `EcsEvent` rules for new contracts.

**Design rule: Loot makes you stronger. Leveling makes you someone.**

issues.title: Make the World Worth Exploring: Town, Landmarks, Dungeons, and Consequences
issues.body:
> **🛰️ Agent flight plan:** `GRAVITY-4` · `WORLD-SPINE` · architecture/content coordination. **MAP-FIRST / VERTICAL-SLICE**: verify existing destinations and their player-facing journeys before creating more terrain. Suitable for staged work; use higher-reasoning review before adding persistent world-discovery contracts.
>
> **Supersedes #146 — “Overworld Is Boring.”** The original observation was correct, but the problem is larger than missing landmark types. **Do not add `GREENLIGHT` until the first implementation slice and dependencies are understood.**

# Make the World Worth Exploring — Town, Landmarks, Dungeons, and Consequences

## The actual problem

**The overworld looks good. It does not yet give the player enough reasons to explore it.**

The missing thing is **not primarily map content**. JSHack has elaborate generated terrain, distinct biomes, a town, authored landmarks, side-dungeon templates, creatures, harvesting, quests, district/entrance pressure, NPCs, and deep loot mechanics. Many exist independently, but the player does not reliably experience them as *places that invite a journey*.

A typical player needs to discover:
1. **A reason to leave town** — a rumor, problem, sightline, strange object, promised treasure, or compelling question.
2. **A direction, not a GPS waypoint** — evidence pointing toward a real reachable location.
3. **A place with an identity** — geography, inhabitants, danger, history, and a particular playable situation.
4. **A decision and a payoff** — something worth risking the trip for, preferably more meaningful than generic gold.
5. **A consequence worth remembering** — return with information/resources, change access or someone's circumstances, or discover a new lead.

**The town should give the wilderness context. The wilderness should give the town something to care about. The dungeon beneath a landmark should feel like part of that same place.**

This is a **world-experience issue**, not a request for more random decorations or more disconnected quests.

## What is already implemented (source verified)

- `src/rules/environment/dungeon/overworld.js` creates a deterministic depth-0, multi-biome map, populates it with biome-dependent creatures and harvesting resources, and calls `placeOverworldLandmarks()`.
- That function currently tries **12 distinct authored landmark types**: ruined watchtower, wayside shrine, abandoned camp, strange grove, bear cave, bat cave, human mine, bandit hideout, old well, collapsed cellar, wolf den, forgotten shrine. A placement can be skipped if no suitable candidate exists.
- The generator excludes candidate landmark centers inside a **52-tile radial distance** of town and spaces landmark centers at least **28 tiles** apart. This creates wilderness, but may also create a considerable **uninformed walk** before a player encounters a reason to care.
- `src/rules/data/buildings/buildingRegistry.js` exposes `LANDMARK_DEFS`, backed by actual tiles/spawns under `src/rules/data/buildings/`; these are not mere names in a wishlist.
- `src/rules/environment/dungeon/underworldRegions.js` already has location-specific regions, including Bear Cave, Bat Cave, Human Mine, Bandit Hideout, Old Well, Collapsed Cellar, Wolf Den and Forgotten Shrine, alongside town-related regions.
- Example: `abandoned_camp.js` already stages a cooking fire, four bandits and an epic/legendary-choice chest. `bandit_hideout.js` contains an entrance targeting its corresponding dungeon template. `forgotten_shrine.js` has a shrine-themed entrance. The *content exists*; discoverability, stakes and differentiated payoff need proof.
- `tests/overworldStructures.test.mjs` checks some authored landmarks and the bandit camp at a fixed seed. It does **not** demonstrate an ordinary player can find a site from town, recognize its name/meaning, engage its activity, return, or see a lasting consequence.
- `src/rules/environment/dungeon/transition.js` already manages region identity, floor transitions, and restoration. `docs/PROGRESSION_RESONANCE_PLAN.md` details reward visibility, journal/tracker paths, and the gap between simulation richness and player motivation.
- #51 covers long-term town/economy/entrance pressure; #166 covers one shortage→contract→production loop. This issue must **compose with** those efforts, not duplicate them.

### Ground truth versus hypotheses

**Verified:** landmark definitions, 12-type placement list, side-region templates, example authored camp/entrance content, tests and reward/quest infrastructure.

**Not yet verified:** whether every landmark is navigably reachable for representative seeds; whether NPCs mention actual sites; whether landmark names appear to players; whether local clues are usable at realistic distances; how often the player encounters one organically; whether all side-dungeon returns preserve the right context. **Audit these, do not assume they work or are absent.**

## World design: places need verbs and connections

Each major location should have a compact **place contract** (authored data using existing conventions where possible):

| Question | Required answer |
| --- | --- |
| What is this place? | Stable identity, optional unique *in-world* name, geographic/biome context |
| Why would I know about it? | A diegetic lead: rumor, map scrap, visible landmark, overheard argument, track, sign, sound, NPC need |
| What can I do there? | At least one meaningful interaction/choice supported by real systems |
| What could happen? | Risk, surprise, conflict, nontrivial mechanical consequence |
| What might I gain? | A legible reward, access, knowledge, resource, relationship, or new destination |
| What changes afterward? | Site state, return visit, NPC conversation, service/access, town interpretation or follow-on lead |
| How is it proven? | Seeded reachable path and automated tests with no fake-only state changes |

This contract should be **small and content-friendly**. Do not introduce a universal new location engine simply to store descriptions.

### A. Town as the information engine

The first visit to the tavern, church, smith, market, or district board should surface **a small number of genuinely discoverable leads** into the world. Leads must point to *actual generated sites* (or supported region entrances), not to randomly invented locations.

Examples of **experience**, not required literal dialogue:
- “The watchtower beyond the stony ridge still flashes on storm nights.”
- “The miners haven't brought iron from the north shaft.”
- “Someone lit a fire in the old bandit camp again.”
- “The priest insists the forgotten shrine is not empty.”

Different roles know different things. Distinguish **rumor / confirmed information / visited discovery**. No NPC omniscience and no mandatory expository tutorial. A player must also be able to stumble onto a site without being sent there.

### B. Wilderness with an invitation gradient

Preserve the attractive large overworld and its wilderness. Improve **the chain of clues and reasons**:
- Recognizable terrain patterns, trails/footprints, disturbed vegetation, light, sound, smoke, tracks, building silhouettes, authored warnings, or environmental aftermath.
- Stronger **near-town hooks** leading toward distant landmarks without revealing everything or shrinking the world.
- Spatially plausible clues using actual location/distance/LOS/hearing knowledge. No unexplained map omniscience.
- Avoid feature confetti and breadcrumb spam: a few memorable destinations beat dozens of interchangeable markers.
- Traversal remains meaningful; do not solve this with mass teleportation, giant objective arrows, or full-map revelation.

### C. Named places rather than generic coordinates

Introduce **stable run-scoped geographic identity** where it adds value:
- A site can become “The Ashen Watch” or “Blackroot Hollow” rather than forever “ruined_watchtower”; naming must be deterministic and **unique per seed among generated sites**.
- Name and identity should survive discovery, return visits, region transitions, and saving/loading. Use canonical site/region identification, not a current entity ID that may be remapped.
- Generated names must fit terrain/biome/landmark identity; do not attach arbitrary names to incompatible locations.
- Keep **unseen / rumored / discovered / resolved** states distinct. An undiscovered place is not automatically revealed because the generator knows its coordinates.
- Prefer extending existing quest journal, dialogue, inspect/tooltip, memory/map or region metadata flows over a new global UI.

A full cartography system is **not a prerequisite**. The player should first be able to remember and recognize places in the tools already available.

### D. Landmarks and dungeons as a continuous journey

A cave entrance should not merely be another staircase into an interchangeable depth-one loot room. The surface, entrance, interior and return should share an authored identity:
- **Bear Cave:** signs of the bear, a plausible den, worthwhile danger, and a reason the player might deliberately seek or avoid it.
- **Bandit Hideout / Abandoned Camp:** signs of occupation, player counterplay, stolen goods or credible prize, and aftermath in local rumors.
- **Forgotten Shrine / Wayside Shrine:** a meaningful choice, deity or ritual interaction, cost or benefit, and a legible consequence.
- **Human Mine:** a location connected to real resource flows and local NPC concerns, without duplicating #166's economy-contract implementation.
- **Old Well / Collapsed Cellar:** a mystery that rewards investigation rather than simply additional stairs.

Use the existing `UNDERWORLD_REGION_TEMPLATES`, landmark spawns, encounter/quest definitions, item/loot registry, and transition mechanics. Don't replace these with a second location system.

### E. Rewards, memory, and aftereffects

A discovery can reward the player through *knowledge*, a tangible artifact, a rare spell/item, service access, a meaningful shortcut, or an actual world change. A generic gold chest at every site is not enough.

The result should be attributable: “I took that risk **because** of the clue; what I found was worth the trip.”

Where supported, the town should acknowledge what happened—changed rumors, a reward/service, altered threat or supply, a return visit behaving differently. Avoid an unreal “Town saved!” message when nothing in the simulation changed.

Prioritize existing catalog and progression systems; verify actual legality, item provenance, canonical loot grants and one-time reward ownership. **Never duplicate loot or restore a cleared chest by crossing an entrance repeatedly.**

## Execution plan — staged, testable, not a world rewrite

### Stage 0 — audit the world that exists (required)

For **all 12 authored landmarks** and relevant town/underworld entrances, produce a compact **place → spawn/seed → reachability → lead → activity → reward → return consequence → persistence/test** matrix. Explicitly classify each dimension as implemented, partial, missing or unverified. Map actual site/region identity and existing player-facing entry points. Include a few representative seeds and a short player-route narrative starting from the actual town spawn.

Do not mistake the presence of `params.landmark` on an entity for a user-visible named or discovered place.

### Stage 1 — prove one complete expedition

Choose the existing **Abandoned Camp / Bandit Hideout** geography if the audit confirms a valid route (alternatively an easier reachable existing site). Create an actual journey:

**Town lead → partial geographic clue → visible approach → meaningful choice/encounter → clearly worthwhile payoff → return acknowledgment / site state retained.**

Ensure the reward is proportional to early-game difficulty; an epic/legendary chest already exists, so consider its balance and prevent an unearned early jackpot.

The site must remain findable without accepting a quest; quests/rumors are invitations, not magic spawn prerequisites.

### Stage 2 — prove a contrasting destination

Repeat the full loop at one **different kind of place** (prefer Forgotten Shrine or Human Mine), with a distinct motivation/verb/reward. This tests whether authoring can scale without hand-coded one-offs. Capture naming/knowledge persistence through revisits and transitions where necessary.

### Stage 3 — connect the wider geography

After two end-to-end successes, generalize only the proven parts: lightweight site metadata, location-aware leads, in-world naming/recognition and discovery memory. Broaden to remaining existing landmarks before adding new landmark types.

Follow-on improvements for real economic change, specific deity challenges, deeper mechanics and authoring skills should link to #166, #165, #157–159 and #156 rather than exploding this implementation.

## Acceptance criteria / measurable play

- [ ] For representative fixed seeds, the audit documents which locations are **actually generated, physically approachable, signaled and reachable**, not just defined.
- [ ] Early in a new run, at least **two actionable leads** are discoverable without wandering blindly for 50+ tiles. No lead points to a nonexistent or unreachable site.
- [ ] Two **different** locations each have a demonstrable, end-to-end expedition: player invitation, clue/approach, place-specific action, reward/consequence, remembered return. At least one is tied to a distinct underworld region.
- [ ] A player who ignores town chatter can still find sites by wandering and environmental evidence.
- [ ] A location's identity and discovered/resolved state are deterministic and survive relevant region transitions, save/load, and entity-ID remapping.
- [ ] Site-specific affordances are represented by real events, items, interaction and loot rules—not only flavor text. Rewards commit at most once.
- [ ] Town/NPC response, when offered, reflects a verified world fact rather than fabricated progress.
- [ ] No softlocked site, blocked entrance, inaccessible cache, full-map spoilers, or crippling expensive pathfinding.
- [ ] Changing terrain/depth doesn't break existing town placement, biome constraints, creature ecology, starter quests, dungeon entrances, or save files.
- [ ] Tests include `tests/overworldStructures.test.mjs`, `tests/overworld.test.mjs`, `tests/overworldCreatureContent.test.mjs`, `tests/questEntranceAccess.test.mjs`, `tests/transition.test.mjs`, `tests/questRuntime.test.mjs`, and focused new seeded expedition/discovery tests. Run relevant Deno guards, **not** the whole runtime suite by default.

## Architectural constraints / effort routing

- `AGENTS.md` is binding: zero-dependency JS/ESM, Deno, no cross-layer imports, deterministic simulation, canonical item/spawn/damage/transition paths, and concrete `EcsEvent` classes for any **new** event contracts. No new world-attached state; store persistent data in the appropriate ECS/region state.
- Don't alter the global economy for a flavor reward, bypass the quest/loot pipeline, or create a second region transition manager.
- Keep generation and player discovery separate: generation knows sites; the player gradually learns them.
- Avoid baking special-case site IDs into general-purpose systems where authored data works.
- **Architecture gate:** if stable site identity/persistence, spatial clue resolution or location↔quest ownership requires a new cross-cutting contract, write a concise source-backed design and an isolated proof before implementation. Escalate that specific decision to higher reasoning instead of letting a medium model improvise new infrastructure.

## Related work and boundaries

- **#146:** original diagnosis, superseded by this issue.
- **#51:** broad substrate/entrance influence/town economy (do not reimplement).
- **#166:** shortage-driven town contracts (do not duplicate).
- **#157 / #159:** mechanic discoverability and encounter learning pattern (reuse).
- **#158:** hydraulics-specific showcase (separate content slice).
- **#165:** deity challenge variation (possible shrine follow-on).
- **#156:** current authoring skills and contracts (coordinate, not block every player-facing win).
- **`docs/PROGRESSION_RESONANCE_PLAN.md`:** reward visibility and payoff direction.

**Design rule: Don't fill the map. Give the player a reason to cross it—and something to carry back.**

issues.title: Necromancer class: Grave Claim — turn fallen enemies into temporary allies
issues.body:
> **🛰️ LUNA-M flight plan:** `GRAVITY-4` · `CORPSE-CONTRACT` · Class data is easy; corpse ownership, summon identity, and death/persistence rules are the actual work. Establish the vertical slice before expanding.

## Concept

# Necromancer 💀 — The Dead Owe You

A fragile battlefield opportunist who sees corpses as *unspent potential*. The Warlock **bargains away living power**; the Necromancer **repossesses the dead**.

Do **not** make this a Warlock with a different starting spell list. Give the Necromancer a recognizably different loop:

**Fight → leave a body → claim it → command the result → choose what to do when it falls.**

Corpse placement, decay, and consumption should matter. Reanimation competes with eating, scavenging, leaving a corpse for another mechanic, and navigating a dangerous room.

## Repo-grounded starting point

- `src/rules/data/classes.js` defines the **Warlock** (22 HP / 65 mana / 13 INT / staff + arcane gloves, currently `agony` + `shadow_bolt`). Reuse its equipment/consumable template; preserve its existing playstyle.
- `src/rules/data/spells.js` already defines `summon_skeleton` (10 mana, **5-turn cast**), `agony`, `drain_life`, `lifetap`, `mark_of_death`, and `shadow_bolt`.
- `src/rules/scripts/spells.js` already creates friendly skeletons on a nearby valid tile, with `PetState`, and `summonedBehaviorSystem.js` already drives summoned allies.
- Corpse identities and on-eat behaviors are real (`src/rules/data/corpseFood.js`); `aiCorpseEatSystem.js` shows how floor corpses can be identified, but is **enemy scavenging**, not a reanimation API.
- `DeathApplied` is the canonical short-lived death record; **do not use the presentation `died` event to create rules-side state**.
- Existing issue #43 discusses *derived semantic intrinsics*. Reuse a suitable current class/trait/virtual-state mechanism; do **not** implement an entire new global intrinsic framework for one class.
- `tests/classes.test.mjs` has an explicit **10-class** assertion; registration, selection, glyph/display, starting inventory, learned spells, and save/load all need coverage.

## Proposed class definition (balance starting point, not sacred constants)

```js
necromancer: {
  id: 'necromancer',
  name: 'Necromancer',
  icon: '💀',
  description: 'A gravebinder who turns fallen enemies into temporary allies. Every corpse is a choice.',
  deityId: 'molkhar', // existing pantheon; do not invent a death deity for this issue
  stats: {
    maxHp: 21,
    maxMana: 60,
    manaRegen: 0.14,
    maxStamina: 80,
    staminaRegen: 2.0,
    intelligence: 14,
    dexterity: 12,
    visionRange: 6,
  },
  equipment: {
    weapon: 'staff_oak',
    armor: null,
    offhand: null,
    gloves: 'gloves_arcane',
    feet: 'shoes_cloth',
  },
  // Reuse Warlock's basic consumable/utility starting kit.
  startingSpells: ['agony', 'summon_skeleton'],
}
```

Keep two normal starting spells for class parity: `agony` provides a viable opening attack; `summon_skeleton` is the identity spell. `drain_life`, `lifetap`, and `mark_of_death` are thematic **existing progression candidates**, not additional free starting powers. Verify how spell learning/loot actually works before promising class-exclusive unlocks.

## Class intrinsic: GRAVE CLAIM 🪦

**The corpse is the reagent. The summon is the payoff.**

A Necromancer can intentionally **Bind Remains** from an eligible, reachable, physical corpse on the ground, transforming it into a temporary allied undead creature. A normal `summon_skeleton` still works without a corpse as an expensive fallback, so the class cannot become helpless on a corpse-free level.

### First playable slice

1. The class-gated affordance `Bind Remains` appears when an eligible corpse is **on the ground, within interaction range**, and there is a valid spawn position. Prefer existing corpse/interact/use/verb contracts; no new hardcoded HUD button.
2. Explicit player choice is required. Binding **consumes exactly one corpse** only when the spawn successfully commits; a blocked tile, unaffordable cost, stale/deleted corpse, or cancelled action must not delete the body.
3. Binding creates one **owner-attributed, controllable, temporary** skeletal ally using canonical spawning + existing summoned AI/command paths. If `summon_skeleton`'s current output is not actually player-commandable or owner-tracked, fix that canonical gap; do not fake it with UI text.
4. Corpse-bound casting should be **tactically faster/cheaper** than conjuring a skeleton from empty ground. Suggested starting tuning: **5 mana and 2 turns when binding**, versus the existing `summon_skeleton` **10 mana and 5 turns**. Adapt to actual spell cost/channel machinery instead of subtracting mana manually after casting.
5. Bound undead have an explicit lifetime (propose **~50 turns** for the first pass) and a small **owned active-minion cap (propose 2)**. The cap applies consistently to both grave-bound and freely summoned skeletons for the Necromancer; no bypass via repeated casting or switching floors.
6. Binding remains should be a tradeoff: it removes a usable food/resource corpse, can be impossible when none exists, and costs a turn/resource commitment under threat.
7. A raised minion must **not leave a fresh eligible corpse** on death/expiry; no self-feeding corpse → minion → corpse loop. No resurrection of player corpses, other summons, quest-critical remains, or shop-owned bodies without explicit policy.
8. Display a legible effect: corpse disappears, allied skeleton appears, player gets a brief message/effect, and the minion's allegiance/expiry/limit is understandable. Do not falsely imply a minion is permanent.

**Stretch goal only after the base loop works:** corpse provenance influences *one* recognizable property of a bound minion (e.g. venomous remains → poison resistance, heavily armored remains → more DR), without creating one-off species clones or a new monster framework. A rat and a bear should eventually feel like different necromantic ingredients, but **do not hold the first playable class hostage to that design**.

### Distinct from other classes

- **Warlock:** direct shadow damage, curses, and risky HP↔mana bargains. The existing Warlock description says it 'commands the dead'; consider a *small wording-only correction* if needed to keep the classes distinct. Do not remove its existing powers.
- **Valkyrie:** already has fate/nearby-death theme in `classes.js`. Necromancer's core should depend on **physically available, explicitly consumed remains**, not passive bonuses whenever a nearby creature dies.
- **Other summon users:** use their existing summon semantics. The corpse discount/rite and cap are **class-gated**, not an accidental global change to every caster of `summon_skeleton`.

## Execution order and design gates

1. **Map current contracts:** class identity at runtime; player class initialization; corpse inventory/ground representation; summon ownership, lifespan, commandability, caster-cost timing; death cleanup; save/load. Confirm existing paths rather than assuming them.
2. **Ship the class baseline:** register class, valid deity, starter gear/items/spells, class-selection icon/description, 11-class assertions, no regressions for Warlock/Valkyrie. Verify the new class can start, survive and cast.
3. **Build one deterministic Bind Remains path:** one known corpse → one valid summon → actual AI movement/attack → expiry; prove player action affordance and actual world mutation.
4. **Enforce resource economics/limits:** cost, casting action, body consumption, max owned summons, expiry/death lifecycle, floor transitions, duplicate/failed action idempotence.
5. **Polish minimally:** VIS/audio/VFX/messages through existing presentation paths. Add corpse-variation only if all above are proved and tests are green.

## Acceptance / executable proof

- [ ] Necromancer appears in character creation and is fully playable, with correct icon, deity, equipment, consumables and two starting spells.
- [ ] Warlock and Valkyrie behavior remain unchanged, except optional Warlock **description-only** disambiguation.
- [ ] Existing `summon_skeleton` and `agony` work for the new class; no accidental rule changes for other classes.
- [ ] A seeded fixture shows an eligible floor corpse → intentional Bind Remains action → corpse consumed once → temporary allied skeleton follows/attacks/accepts relevant commands.
- [ ] No corpse, no valid spawn tile, insufficient mana, expired corpse, or an exceeded minion cap fails clearly **without losing items or spending resources incorrectly**.
- [ ] Owned summon cap, duration, death and reload/floor-transition behavior are correct; summoned allies do not leave infinitely reusable eligible corpses.
- [ ] Focused Deno tests cover class registration, cast/bind flow, owner attribution, action economy, no duplicate reward/consumption, minion AI, and save/load.
- [ ] Relevant existing tests: `tests/classes.test.mjs`, `tests/classDisplayData.test.mjs`, `tests/summonedAttack.test.mjs`, `tests/petBehavior.test.mjs`, `tests/corpseUseProc.test.mjs`, `tests/savegameLoad.test.mjs`; add a focused necromancer test module. Run architectural guards if new event/extension glue is touched.

## Architecture limits

Obey `AGENTS.md`: Deno/ESM, no new world-attached state, deterministic simulation, canonical spawn/item/intent paths, rules/display separation, scheduler-owned system ordering, and concrete `EcsEvent` classes for **new** events. Don't implement new behavior by listening to a UI/audio notification or making the spell script mutate unrelated systems through event side channels.

**Scope control:** one *complete* Necromancer + Grave Claim interaction first, not a general summoning overhaul or an undead bestiary.

**A Warlock steals life. A Necromancer refuses to let the dead leave.**
